clue.text: Catholic possesses blue woolly vestment

parts.note: to possess something is to have it, so possesses gives has

indicators.note: woolly means muddled or vague, telling us to jumble the letters of blue

explanation.surface: A Catholic priest owns a fuzzy blue garment for church services.
explanation.walkthrough: 'woolly' sounds like a description of the vestment's fabric, but it is the signal to jumble the colour word.
explanation.definitionFit: A chasuble is the sleeveless outer robe a priest wears to celebrate Mass, a kind of liturgical vestment.

clue.text: Be indulgent with cook

definitions.meaning: to simmer eggs gently in water just below boiling

explanation.definitionFit: To coddle is both to pamper a person and to poach eggs gently in hot water.

clue.text: Without exception, say law must be amended

indicators.note: amended means altered, so the letters of say and law are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A lawyer insists a statute needs changing in every single case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'must be amended' rearranges SAY plus LAW.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done without exception happens every time, at all times.

clue.text: Pawnbroker accepting article that's grubby

parts.note: uncle is old slang for a pawnbroker
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A pawnbroker takes in some item that turns out to be dirty.
explanation.walkthrough: Calling a pawnbroker 'uncle' is old British slang. 'accepting' is only a link here, not a container signal: the article simply follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Unclean and grubby are synonyms, both meaning dirty.

clue.text: Slip of the lips?

parts.note: a speech defect, a sort of slip made with the tongue and lips, and the letters of slip itself rearranged

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark points to a speech fault where s sounds come out as th; it also happens that the four letters of Slip can be shuffled to give it.
explanation.definitionFit: A lisp is a speech defect in which s is pronounced like th, a slip of the tongue against the teeth.

clue.text: Calm contralto in tartan

indicators.note: in tells us the contralto letter sits inside the tartan word

parts.note: plaid is a tartan cloth
C is the abbreviation for contralto in music

explanation.surface: A deep-voiced singer remains serene wearing a kilt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts C inside PLAID.
explanation.definitionFit: Placid means peaceful and untroubled, a synonym of calm.

clue.text: The French medicine find's just little bits of lava

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'The French medicine find's just little bits of lava': LA + PILL gives LAPILL, and nothing in 'find's just' supplies the final I; a word such as 'I' or 'one' looks lost in OCR.
annotationWithheld.clue: The French medicine find's just little bits of lava

clue.text: Double feature to face for good health, drinkers say

indicators.note: double tells us the facial feature appears twice in a row

parts.note: the chin is a feature belonging to the face

explanation.surface: A movie double bill on the face, or so drinkers raising glasses say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Double' repeats CHIN. The toast is said when glasses are raised.
explanation.definitionFit: Chin-chin is a jolly toast offered before drinking, wishing everyone good health.

clue.text: Reds fancy simple horse training method

indicators.note: fancy as an adjective means elaborate, so the letters of Reds are arranged in a new way

parts.note: a simple is an old word for a medicinal herb, and sage is one

explanation.surface: Communists favour a straightforward way to train horses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fancy' rearranges REDS into DRES. 'simple' is a noun here: an old word for a medicinal herb, such as SAGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Dressage is the competitive equestrian discipline of training a horse to perform precise movements.

clue.text: Depressed, having moulted

definitions.meaning: having shed its soft feathers, as a bird does

explanation.definitionFit: Downcast means dejected; split, down cast describes a bird that has shed its fluffy feathers.

clue.text: Impish metamorphosis for priest

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Impish metamorphosis for priest': the anagram of priest gives the answer, but 'Impish' is an adjective and cannot define the noun; the setter probably wrote 'Imp is', which the scan cannot confirm.

clue.text: An aid to a climber or a one-legged jumper?

definitions.meaning: a tall pole supporting climbing hop plants
whimsically, a stick for someone who hops

explanation.definitionFit: Hop-poles support the climbing hop vine; the joke reads it as a pole for a person hopping on one leg.

clue.text: Namely, the sort of people you get outside the church

definitions.text: people you get outside the church

indicators.note: sort as a verb means arrange, so the letters of Namely are put in order again

explanation.surface: Ordinary folk, in other words, are the kind found beyond the church walls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sort of' rearranges NAMELY.
explanation.definitionFit: Laymen are ordinary members of a faith who are not clergy, so they stand outside the ordained church.

clue.text: Using these devices, take a boat out on parts of the canals

definitions.text: Using these devices, take a boat out on parts of the canals

parts.note: to take a boat out with oars is to row
locks are the gated sections of a canal that raise and lower boats

explanation.surface: A guide to rowing along a canal, gates and all.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines the oar supports while ROW and LOCKS build them.
explanation.definitionFit: Rowlocks are the pivots on a boat's gunwale that hold the oars as you row.

clue.text: Ungenerous to take Mollie Malone's job, say?

indicators.note: say tells us the words are spoken out loud to give a word that sounds alike

parts.note: Molly Malone, of the Dublin folk song, wheeled a barrow selling cockles and mussels, so her job was to sell fish

explanation.surface: Is it mean to take over the fishmonger's job from a famous Dublin street seller?
explanation.walkthrough: Molly Malone is the fishmonger of the Irish song 'Cockles and Mussels'. Spoken, sell fish sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Selfish and ungenerous both describe someone unwilling to share with others.

clue.text: Adventurous to gain access using a jemmy?

parts.note: to get in is to enter
a jemmy is a burglar's crowbar, used for prising things open

explanation.surface: A burglar who levers a door open to get in is certainly bold.
explanation.walkthrough: A jemmy is a burglar's short crowbar.
explanation.definitionFit: Enterprising means showing initiative and readiness to take on bold new ventures.

clue.text: Requires fifty, loses point, nutty creature!

indicators.note: nutty means crazy, telling us to mix up the remaining letters
loses signals that a letter is dropped from the word Requires

parts.note: E (east) is a compass point
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: An excited animal demands fifty nuts and misses the point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loses' removes the compass point from the first word, leaving RQUIRES, which 'nutty' shuffles to SQUIRRE before the Roman numeral is added.
explanation.definitionFit: A squirrel is a bushy-tailed tree-dwelling rodent, a small wild creature.

clue.text: Get the leaver to try a height

parts.note: to try something is to test it
a tor is a rocky hill or peak

explanation.surface: Encourage someone departing to attempt to climb a summit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaver' here is one who leaves property in a will. A TOR is a rocky hilltop, common on Dartmoor.
explanation.definitionFit: A testator is a person who makes a will, bequeathing property to heirs.

clue.text: Reigning lady golf champion?

parts.note: a woman who rules the golf course with her clubs, also a court card in the suit of clubs

explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a female golf champion; the answer is a playing card from the clubs suit.
explanation.definitionFit: This court card is the female royal of the clubs suit, here imagined as queen of the golf clubs.

clue.text: It's turbulent in large water pipe

indicators.note: turbulent means stormy and disordered, so the letters of in large are thrown about

explanation.surface: Things get choppy inside a big plumbing pipe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turbulent' rearranges IN LARGE.
explanation.definitionFit: A nargile is a hookah, a smoking pipe that draws smoke through water.

clue.text: Grating concealed in, mountain greenery

indicators.note: concealed in tells us the grating word is hidden inside the mountain word

parts.note: ben is a Scottish word for a mountain, as in Ben Nevis
a rack is a grating or framework of bars

explanation.surface: A grille hidden among mountain foliage.
explanation.walkthrough: The comma tempts you to read 'Grating concealed in' as a hidden word; instead 'concealed in' puts one synonym inside another. BEN is Scots for mountain.
explanation.definitionFit: Bracken is a large fern covering hillsides, so it counts as green vegetation.

clue.text: Prune I throw out — it's green

indicators.note: to throw out the letters is to scatter them into a new order

explanation.surface: Discarding a dried plum because it is not yet ready.
explanation.walkthrough: 'throw out' rearranges PRUNE I.
explanation.definitionFit: Unripe fruit is not yet mature, and green is a common word for that state.

clue.text: Ungroomed, a horse about to attempt to unseat its rider?

indicators.note: about tells us the attempt word goes around the horse letters

parts.note: a horse that shies starts suddenly, which can unseat a rider; a shy is also an attempt
gee-gee, GG, is a child's word for a horse

explanation.surface: An unkempt horse is about to throw off its jockey.
explanation.walkthrough: SHY goes 'about' A GG; GG is nursery language for a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: Shaggy describes long, untidy, unkempt hair or fur.

clue.text: Concern in repairing street

indicators.note: repairing means fixing up, so the letters of in street are rebuilt

explanation.surface: Worries about road works in the high street.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests roadworks, but 'in' simply stands at the front as written, and 'repairing' turns the road word into TEREST.
explanation.definitionFit: An interest is a matter that concerns or involves you.

clue.text: Start with a picnic

indicators.note: with here means holding, so the letter a is placed inside the picnic word

parts.note: a picnic is a lunch eaten outdoors

explanation.surface: Kicking off a day out with a meal on the grass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' has LUNCH holding A.
explanation.definitionFit: To launch an enterprise is to start or begin it.

clue.text: Sound, sense to hunt for the Indian

indicators.note: Sound tells us the word for hunting is spoken out loud to give a soundalike

parts.note: to seek is to hunt or search for

explanation.surface: Healthy instinct leads someone to search for a person from India.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' could be the adjective meaning healthy; it signals that the word is spoken.
explanation.definitionFit: A Sikh follows Sikhism, the faith founded in the Punjab region of India.

clue.text: Being concerned with the queue to find a selling method

parts.note: re means about or concerning
the tail of something is a line trailing behind, like a queue

explanation.surface: Worrying about the waiting line to find a way of selling.
explanation.walkthrough: RE means about, as at the top of a business letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Retail is the sale of goods direct to the public, a method of selling.

clue.text: Select fish for preservation

parts.note: to select is to pick
ling is a sea fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: Choosing a fish to cure.
explanation.walkthrough: LING is a long cod-like sea fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Pickling is preserving food in brine or vinegar, a means of preservation.

clue.text: Ruled king's corruption was concealed for no good reason

definitions.text: was concealed for no good reason

indicators.note: corruption means spoiling, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: The rotten reign of a monarch was kept secret for shady motives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'corruption' rearranges RULED plus K.
explanation.definitionFit: To lurk is to hide or wait out of sight, typically with sinister intent.

clue.text: Mean to house Nunhead church archives

indicators.note: to house means to contain, so the stingy word holds the other letters inside

parts.note: chary can mean sparing or stingy
the head, or first letter, of nun
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Stingy to hold onto records from a south London church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nunhead' is a real south London district, but here it means the head of nun. 'to house' puts that letter and the Church of England inside a word for stingy.
explanation.definitionFit: Chancery was the office of public records, where the archives of the Crown's court were kept.
